text:
sam-customer: Hi team — our app just started seeing 2x requests and much higher tail latency. We're also getting extra billing for duplicated invocations. Not sure if SDK issue or your routing. Repro: users in EU suddenly hit US region.

maya-support: sorry about that — can you paste a short SDK config and a couple logs? which SDK version?

sam-customer: Using redwood-js v0.9.2, default client config. Here's the trimmed log for one request (timestamps removed):
```
client: send request -> region=eu-west-1
client: hedged_request dispatched to eu-west-1 and us-east-1
resp(us-east-1): 200 OK, 120ms
resp(eu-west-1): timeout -> client retried to us-east-1 again
billing: charge recorded for both invocations
```

maya-support: thanks. That log suggests the SDK did a hedged request to two regions and both succeeded/charged. Can you confirm hedgedRequests flag?

sam-customer: yes, we enabled hedgedRequests for latency, config snippet:
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({
  region: 'eu-west-1',
  hedgedRequests: true,
  hedgeWindowMs: 50,
  timeoutMs: 300
});
```

raj-sdk: pinging in — short version: with hedgedRequests enabled and a small hedgeWindowMs, the client will send parallel attempts to fallback regions per our routing fallback policy. If both servers accept the request you can end up with multiple server-side executions. Normally we dedupe at gateway but only if idempotency keys are present.

raj-sdk: quick mitigation: set hedgedRequests:false or increase hedgeWindowMs and add an idempotency key on write operations. Also we should examine why routing picked us-east-1 for an EU client.

tess-sre: I pulled our gateway logs for the trace id you sent (trace=tr_8bcd...). Our router saw the request with header X-Home-Region: eu-west-1 but also observed a failed health check on the eu pool at the moment. Fallback policy routed attempts to nextPreferredRegion (us-east-1) for capacity. Both attempts completed because the eu instance recovered after the hedge was already sent.

leo-eng: adding infra context — we had a transient control-plane flapping for eu-west region at 2024-08-21T14:22Z (short outage ~30s). Routing policy will hedge to alternate regions during those windows. We should have prevented double execution for non-idempotent endpoints; that's a gap.

maya-support: for immediate customer relief: we'll issue a billing credit for duplicate charges and open an internal incident to add server-side dedupe or require idempotency enforcement for hedged paths. Filing billing ticket now.

billing-bot: Ticket BG-4721 created: refund pending review. Customer: sam-customer.

sam-customer: appreciate quick action. For long term, can you advise SDK defaults? We expected hedgedRequests to be safe by default.

raj-sdk: agreed we should make safer defaults. Action items: 1) default hedgedRequests=false for mutating endpoints, 2) SDK to auto-generate and attach idempotency keys for POST-like calls, 3) runtime to reject double-exec for short windows if identical idempotency key seen. I'll open RFC and a patch.

tess-sre: ops action: set eu routing healthcheck stricter (avoid premature fallback) and add metric to detect double-hit rates.

maya-support: closing loop for now — refund ticket filed, eng has assigned followups (RFC+patch). Sam, if you want immediate stop, set hedgedRequests:false and redeploy client.

sam-customer: done, disabled hedging and latency returned to normal. Thanks all :thumbsup:

leo-eng: flagging postmortem and cc-ing product.

maya-support: marking resolved for support; will keep you posted on BG-4721 and the eng RFC.

sam-customer: thanks — appreciate the fast turnaround.
